questions.stem: The SI unit of the moment of a force is the
questions.explanation: Moment is force multiplied by perpendicular distance, so its unit is newton × metre = N m. Although a joule is also numerically N × m, the joule is reserved for energy, where the distance is measured along the direction of the force rather than perpendicular to it.

distractorRationale.a: The newton is the unit of force alone, with no distance factor
distractorRationale.c: The joule has the same dimensions but is used for work and energy, not turning effect
distractorRationale.d: N/m is the unit of a spring constant, obtained by dividing rather than multiplying

questions.stem: The moment of a force about a point is defined as the product of the force and the

options.text: time for which the force acts
distance moved along the line of action of the force
perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force
mass of the body on which the force acts

questions.explanation: Only the component of the distance at right angles to the force produces turning. That is why pulling straight along a spanner handle, where the perpendicular distance is zero, gives no turning effect at all.

distractorRationale.a: Force multiplied by time is impulse, which changes momentum rather than causing rotation
distractorRationale.b: Force multiplied by distance along its own line is work done, measured in joules
distractorRationale.d: Mass appears in F = ma, not in the definition of a moment

questions.stem: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?

options.text: It is not a lever at all

questions.explanation: In a wheelbarrow the wheel is the fulcrum, the soil in the pan is the load and the hands lift at the handles. The load therefore lies between the fulcrum and the effort, which defines a second-class lever, and this is why the effort needed is less than the load.

distractorRationale.a: First class needs the fulcrum in the middle, as in a see-saw; here the wheel is at one end
distractorRationale.c: Third class needs the effort in the middle, as in a pair of tongs
distractorRationale.d: A wheelbarrow is a rigid bar turning about a fulcrum, which is exactly a lever

questions.stem: A force of 20 N acts at right angles to a spanner at a perpendicular distance of 0.50 m from the nut. Calculate the moment of the force about the nut. Give your answer in newton metres.
questions.explanation: Moment $= F \times d_{\perp} = 20 \times 0.50 = 10\ \text{N m}$. The distance must already be in metres for the answer to come out in newton metres; using 50 cm directly would give the wrong numerical value.

questions.stem: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its 50 cm mark. A weight of 2.0 N hangs at the 20 cm mark. Calculate how far from the pivot a weight of 4.0 N must hang on the other side to balance the rule. Give your answer in centimetres.
questions.explanation: The rule is uniform and pivoted at its centre, so its own weight has no moment. The anticlockwise moment is $2.0 \times (50 - 20) = 2.0 \times 30 = 60\ \text{N cm}$. Setting $4.0 \times d = 60$ gives $d = 15\ \text{cm}$, which is the 65 cm mark.

questions.stem: A boy of mass 40 kg sits 2.0 m from the pivot of a see-saw. A girl of mass 50 kg sits on the other side. For the see-saw to balance, she must sit at a distance of
questions.explanation: Applying the principle of moments with weights proportional to masses: $40 \times 2.0 = 50 \times d$, so $d = \frac{80}{50} = 1.6\ \text{m}$. Since the girl is heavier, she must sit closer to the pivot, which the answer confirms. The value of g cancels from both sides.

distractorRationale.b: Assumes equal distances, which would only balance equal masses
distractorRationale.c: Inverted the ratio, using 50 × 2.0 ÷ 40 — this places the heavier person further out
distractorRationale.d: Doubled the boy's distance with no use of the masses at all

questions.stem: A uniform beam AB of length 4.0 m and weight 200 N rests horizontally on supports at its two ends. A load of 600 N is placed 1.0 m from A. Calculate the reaction at support B. Give your answer in newtons.
questions.explanation: Take moments about A, which removes the unknown reaction at A. The beam's own 200 N weight acts at the midpoint, 2.0 m from A, so $R_B \times 4.0 = (600 \times 1.0) + (200 \times 2.0) = 1000\ \text{N m}$, giving $R_B = 250\ \text{N}$. Checking, $R_A = 800 - 250 = 550\ \text{N}$, and the support nearer the load carries more, as it should.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a third-class lever?

options.text: A pair of tongs used to pick up hot coals
A crowbar levering up a crate

questions.explanation: In a pair of tongs the hinge is the fulcrum at one end, the coal is the load at the far end, and the fingers squeeze somewhere in between. Effort between fulcrum and load defines a third-class lever, which is why tongs need more effort than the load they hold but give delicate control.

distractorRationale.a: Scissors have the pivot between the effort and the load, making them first class
distractorRationale.b: A nutcracker has the nut between the hinge and the hands, making it second class
distractorRationale.d: A crowbar pivots on a point between the effort and the crate, making it first class

questions.stem: A uniform metre rule of weight 1.5 N balances horizontally on a knife edge placed at its 40 cm mark when a small weight W hangs at the 10 cm mark. Calculate W. Give your answer in newtons.
questions.explanation: The rule is uniform, so its 1.5 N weight acts at the 50 cm mark, which is $50 - 40 = 10\ \text{cm}$ on the far side of the pivot, giving a clockwise moment of $1.5 \times 10 = 15\ \text{N cm}$. The hanging weight is $40 - 10 = 30\ \text{cm}$ from the pivot on the other side, so $W \times 30 = 15$, giving $W = 0.5\ \text{N}$.

questions.stem: A crowbar 1.2 m long is used to lift a crate. The fulcrum is placed 0.20 m from the end that touches the crate, and an effort of 100 N is applied at the far end. Calculate the maximum load that can just be lifted. Give your answer in newtons.
questions.explanation: The effort arm is $1.2 - 0.20 = 1.0\ \text{m}$ and the load arm is $0.20\ \text{m}$. Applying the principle of moments, $\text{load} \times 0.20 = 100 \times 1.0$, so the load is $\frac{100}{0.20} = 500\ \text{N}$. The crowbar multiplies the effort five times because the effort arm is five times the load arm.

questions.stem: Two equal and opposite parallel forces act on a rigid body along different lines of action. The body will

options.text: both rotate and accelerate in a straight line

questions.explanation: The two forces cancel as vectors, so the resultant force and hence the linear acceleration is zero. But because they act along different lines, their moments about any point add rather than cancel, producing a net turning effect. Such a pair is called a couple.

distractorRationale.a: The first condition of equilibrium is met but the second is not, so the body turns
distractorRationale.b: Linear acceleration requires a non-zero resultant force, and here the resultant is zero
distractorRationale.d: There is no resultant force, so there can be no linear acceleration
